subject: anatomy
title: Small and large intestine: vessels, appendix and watershed zones

steps.tx: The **jejunum** forms the proximal two fifths of the small intestine and the **ileum** the distal three fifths, with no sharp line between them. The jejunum is thicker, wider and has tall, closely packed plicae circulares. It has fewer arcades, with one or two long vasa recta, while the ileum has four or five arcades with shorter vasa recta.
steps.say: The jejunum forms the proximal two fifths of the small intestine and the ileum the distal three fifths, with no sharp line between them. The jejunum is thicker and wider, and has tall, closely packed plicae circulares. It has one or two arcades sending out long vasa recta, whereas the ileum has four or five arcades with shorter vasa recta.

steps.tx: The superior mesenteric artery supplies the midgut, from the second part of the duodenum to the proximal half of the transverse colon. Its **ileocolic**, **right colic** and **middle colic** branches join the **marginal artery of Drummond**, a continuous arcade along the inner border of the colon. The inferior mesenteric artery supplies the left third of the transverse colon, the descending and sigmoid colon, and the upper rectum.
steps.say: The superior mesenteric artery supplies the midgut, from the second part of the duodenum to the proximal half of the transverse colon. Its ileocolic, right colic and middle colic branches join the marginal artery of Drummond, a continuous arcade along the inner border of the colon. The inferior mesenteric artery supplies the left third of the transverse colon, the descending and sigmoid colon, and the upper rectum.

steps.tx: The **watershed areas** of the colon are weak points where the marginal artery anastomoses are incomplete. **Griffith point** lies at the splenic flexure, between the superior and inferior mesenteric systems. **Sudeck point** lies at the rectosigmoid junction, between the inferior mesenteric and internal iliac arteries. The splenic flexure is the most ischaemia-prone site.
steps.say: The watershed areas of the colon are weak points where marginal artery anastomoses are incomplete. Griffith point lies at the splenic flexure, between the superior and inferior mesenteric systems. Sudeck point lies at the rectosigmoid junction, between the inferior mesenteric and internal iliac arteries. The splenic flexure is the most ischaemia-prone site.

steps.tx: The **appendix** arises from the posteromedial caecal wall, about 2 cm below the ileocaecal junction. Its base is fixed but its tip varies. The **retrocaecal** position is commonest, at about 65 percent, followed by the **pelvic** position at about 30 percent. The appendix is supplied by the appendicular artery, a branch of the posterior caecal artery from the ileocolic artery.

steps.tx: The **mesentery** varies along the colon. The transverse and sigmoid colon have mesenteries, and the ascending and descending colon are largely retroperitoneal. The **rectum** lies retroperitoneal below the rectosigmoid junction. The **superior rectal vein** drains into the inferior mesenteric vein, while the inferior rectal vein drains into the internal pudendal vein.

vis.alt: Two columns separating colon parts that have a mesentery and are mobile (transverse colon, sigmoid colon, appendix) from parts that are retroperitoneal and fixed (ascending colon, descending colon).
vis.caption: Transverse and sigmoid colon hang on mesocolons; ascending and descending colon are plastered to the back wall.
